newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Friday were seen selling steady to $0.50 per cwt lower than Thursday's values, pressured by weak pork prices and adequate hog numbers, dealers and packer buyers said.

Marketings on Thursday in southern Minnesota and northern Iowa were slowed by sleet and snow, which made travel difficult in some areas, buyers said. Some said they were unable to buy the hogs Thursday they needed for Friday's operations and would be buying early Friday to round out the day's slaughter.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs at the plant could range $47.00 to $48.00, sources there said.
Illinois prices at plants could range from $47.00 to $48.00 and Indiana/Ohio top prices could span $47.00 to $47.50, sources in those areas said.
The weather in Minnesota and Iowa was expected to improve enough by early Friday to allow packers to gather the hogs they need for Friday and Saturday slaughter, sources said.
Increased hog slaughter this week and subsequent greater pork supplies compared with last week, contributed to lower pork prices, they said.
Hog slaughter on Thursday was estimated at 354,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 1.372 million head, above 1.368 million a week ago and below 1.431 million a year ago, USDA said.
